The word afghan has a few distinct meanings depending on context and capitalization. Here is each one, explained fully.
1. A soft knitted or crocheted blanket (lowercase "afghan")

This is the most common everyday meaning of the word in modern usage, especially in American English.

An afghan is a warm, cozy blanket — typically hand-knitted or crocheted (meaning it's made by looping yarn together using needles or a hook, rather than woven on a loom). It is usually made from wool or acrylic yarn and often features colorful stripes, geometric patterns, or decorative stitching. It is generally soft and somewhat thick.

Afghans are not heavy industrial blankets. They are more like decorative throws — the kind you drape over the back of a sofa or armchair, or wrap around your shoulders while sitting indoors. They are associated with warmth, comfort, and handmade craftsmanship. Grandmothers knitting afghans for their grandchildren is a classic image in American culture.

In size, an afghan is typically big enough to cover a person sitting down, but it's not as large as a full bed blanket. It can also be used as a baby blanket.

Example sentences:

  • "She curled up on the couch under a colorful afghan."
  • "My grandmother spent months crocheting an afghan as a gift."

When written with a capital A, an Afghan refers to a person who is from Afghanistan — a country in South Central Asia. It is a demonym, meaning it identifies someone by their nationality or place of origin, similar to how "Indian" refers to someone from India.

The word can be used both as a noun ("He is an Afghan") and as an adjective ("Afghan culture"). The noun use simply means: a citizen or native of Afghanistan.

Example sentences:

  • "Several Afghans were resettled in the city after the war."
  • "She is an Afghan who moved to Canada in 2005."

In informal or casual speech, Afghan is also used as a shorthand for an Afghan hound — a specific breed of dog.

The Afghan hound is a tall, slender, aristocratic-looking dog with a long, flowing, silky coat of fur. It resembles a creature out of a fairy tale — elegant and graceful in appearance. The breed is ancient and was originally used for hunting in the mountainous regions of Afghanistan, where it needed both speed and endurance. Today it is primarily kept as a show dog or companion pet.

When someone says "She has a beautiful Afghan," they typically mean this dog.

Example sentences:

  • "The Afghan pranced across the show ring with its long coat flowing."
  • "Afghans are known for being fast runners but somewhat aloof in personality."
How to tell which meaning is intended

• If someone is talking about knitting, yarn, crafts, warmth, or something draped on a sofa → they mean the blanket.
  • If someone is talking about people, nationalities, refugees, or a country → they mean a person from Afghanistan.
  • If someone is talking about dogs, dog shows, or pets → they mean the Afghan hound.

Context almost always makes it perfectly clear which meaning is being used.
